Subject: Intake: dev control index and targeted artefacts for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for agreeing to a lightweight intake. To finish our triage for BankCo's SIG review we need: an index of controls mapped to the SIG/CAIQ Secure Development questions, a small representative sample of PRs and CI runs showing gating and secrets scanning, and any recent change-approval logs for production-impacting releases (last 6 months).

Can you provide: 1) a CSV with mapping (control id, location, owner, evidence path), 2) a short list (5-8) of PRs with run IDs we can pull, and 3) a brief note on secrets handling (KMS/HSM, ephemeral tokens, what is rotated and frequency)?

If you have a redlined or annotated doc pointing to where each claim is supported that would save time. We prefer zip/CSV and short text excerpts rather than large bundles. Deadline: end of day Wednesday Pacific if possible.

Pauline
Assessment Lead
Acme Assessments

Pauline — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. High-level summary here so you have context while we gather files:

- Control index: we'll export a compact CSV mapping our internal control IDs (RF-*) to SIG/CAIQ question numbers and to canonical evidence locations (Drive + JIRA attachments).
- PR sample: we'll provide 6 PRs across three services (api-gateway, inference-runtime, console-ui) that show branch protection, mandatory code review, and pipeline gating. For each PR we'll include CI run IDs and a brief narrative of why it demonstrates the control.
- Secrets handling: Redwood uses customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; hosted uses KMS + hardware-backed key wrapping for symmetric secrets. Short summary: ephemeral CI tokens are minted per-run, scanned secrets are blocked by pre-merge checks, and deployments require a two-person approval for prod-impacting jobs.

I'm attaching an initial index CSV and a trimmed CI logs excerpt for a representative merge. Irene and Jonas — can you review the redline we're preparing and add any missing PR samples? I'll consolidate and send the redline doc back before EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Looping in Jordan for the PR sampling — Jordan, I've picked three PRs that demonstrate PR gating + secrets detection (see CSV stub). Jonas, please add one runtime hotfix and one console UI feature PR to round out service coverage.

Notes for Pauline/Assessor:
- Secrets: we enforce pre-merge scanning via SCA hooks (Trivy + custom regex) and block merges when high-risk findings hit. CI tokens: ephemeral tokens issued by Vault Agent with TTL of 10 minutes for jobs that require privileged access; bootstrap tokens are rotated nightly.
- PR gating: branch protection enforces at least two approvers for prod branches, combined with required status checks. Merge queue processed by our internal bot which verifies CI artifacts and signatures.
- Change approvals: production deployments require a runbook entry and sign-off using our change-approval Jira workflow (fields: reviewer, impact, rollback_plan). Older runs are archived in the change-audits index.

I'll export the PR list and short annotated run transcripts by 11:30am PT and drop them in the Drive link.

Irene Choi
Sr. Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Dev controls index + redline (submitted)

Pauline / team — attaching the consolidated items as requested. Summary of what is in the package: 

1) dev_controls_index.csv — concise mapping (control_id, redwood_claim, SIG/CAIQ ref, evidence_path).
2) pr-sample-list.csv — six PRs with links, reviewers, CI run IDs, and short notes on gating and findings.
3) ci_pipeline_logs_excerpt.txt — redacted CI run showing pre-merge checks, secret-scan output, and artifact signing steps.
4) redline_controls.docx — a short redline where we call out the exact file or run that supports each numbered claim.

Key callouts:
- Our secrets policy: ephemeral job tokens minted from Vault with automatic revocation; long-lived keys are in KMS with envelope encryption and HSM-backed wrapping in the Private deployment.
- PR gate enforcement: 2 approvers + passing status checks + artifact signature verification.
- Emergency change path: when a rollback or fast patch is required, an emergency PR must still include a runbook entry and two on-call signoffs; we retain a separate audit trail for emergency approvals.

We've also included Drive links in the redline where you can open the CI run JSON logs if you need deeper artifacts. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with our security engineering team this week to step through one of the PRs live.

Best,
Priyom Das
Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
